title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Elemental powders of a CoCrFeNiMo_x high‐entropy alloy mixed with Ni, MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3 additives
recollection.intervention: Guess: High‐energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) to consolidate the composite under controlled temperature and pressure
recollection.structure: Guess: A dense composite with a FCC high‐entropy alloy matrix embedding finely dispersed Ni, MoS2 lamellae, Ag nanoparticles, and Cr2O3 platelets
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Under sliding, the MoS2 and Ag phases smear to form a low‐shear‐strength tribofilm on the surface, while Cr2O3 provides hardness reinforcement and the HEA matrix supplies toughness
recollection.results: Guess: Achieved a low friction coefficient of ~0.08 under dry sliding at 2 N load and a wear rate on the order of 1×10⁻⁷ mm³/(N·m), representing a 50 % improvement over a CoCrFeNi baseline

score.note: The recollection correctly gestures toward ball milling/SPS processing, an FCC HEA matrix, and Ag/MoS2-derived low-shear tribofilms, but it misses the central intervention of varying Mo content and the key Mo-induced lattice distortion and σ-phase formation. It also omits the temperature-dependent oxide/silver-molybdate glaze mechanism. The claimed friction coefficient, load, wear rate, and baseline improvement are unsupported and substantially inconsistent with the reported results.
